title: Reserve Conductor Slate — Compact Autoscale Knobs & Health Insights
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design a compact control surface within the Redwood Console for dedicated GPU reserves that surfaces per-pool health signals, quick autoscale knobs, and burst authority controls. The component should be usable in narrow sidebars and full-page fleet views and wire into rollout & cost telemetry.
context: Customers running Dedicated capacity need a lightweight, actionable controls panel to react to transient demand (burst) and tune autoscale policies without navigating to full policy editors. Existing designs are large and geared to single-cluster workflows; this work aims to create a condensed, reusable slate for multi-pool views and operational runbooks.
goals: Provide an at-a-glance health strip (CPU/GPU util, queue depth, thermal events) for each pool
Expose 3-4 primary autoscale controls with immediate simulation feedback (min/max, target utilization, burst allowance)
Allow fast manual burst triggers and safe rollback buttons tied to rollout policies
Surface cost impact estimate before applying changes (per-minute and hourly breakdown)
Create a compact responsive layout for sidebar and modal contexts
deliverables: Figma prototype: compact slate (sidebar + modal variants)
Handoff doc with API contract notes for telemetry signals
Accessibility checklist and keyboard flow spec
Design review notes and iteration log
acceptance_criteria: Prototype contains both sidebar (300–420px) and modal (900px) layouts
Health strip displays at least 5 telemetry points with tooltips and drill-through links
Autoscale knobs have inline simulation showing expected latency/cost delta
Manual burst action requires confirm flow and documents estimated cost impact
Design tokens provided and annotated for dev; component passes a11y contrast and keyboard tests
